newsitem.title: USA: Honda to build S. Carolina plant - local officials.
newsitem.headline: Honda to build S. Carolina plant - local officials.

text.p: Honda Motor Co Ltd plans to build a $40 million plant in South Carolina that will produce all-terrain vehicles and personal watercraft, local officials said Thursday.

Henry Peoples, mayor of Timmonsville, said Honda on Monday planned to announce plans to build the facility in his town, near Florence. It is expected to be built in five phases, with about 600 workers employed in the first stage, he said.
The first-phase products will include the watercraft and motorcycle-like all-terrain vehicles, but Peoples said Honda has not disclosed products for later phases of the facility.
Honda currently does not build personal watercraft anywhere in the world. The U.S. market for such watercraft has grown rapidly in recent years, but recently has shown some signs of leveling off.
Earlier, South Carolina Sen. Ernest Hollings, a Democrat, discussed the plant during a meeting of the Senate Commerce Committee. His office said the facility would emloy about 700 people.

Peoples said the state, county and town governments have assembled an incentive package for Honda, but he declined to disclose its value. The plant will be strategically located near the intersection of Interstate highways 95 and 20.
"We are just as excited as we can be," Peoples said of the project.
